content: Self-condensation is an organic chemical reaction in which a single compound containing a carbonyl group functions simultaneously as both the electrophile and the nucleophile during an aldol condensation process. This reaction is also referred to as a symmetrical aldol condensation, distinguishing it from a mixed aldol condensation, where the electrophile and nucleophile are two different chemical species. For instance, two molecules of acetone can undergo condensation to form a single compound known as mesityl oxide. This reaction typically occurs in the presence of an ion exchange resin. In synthetic chemistry, self-condensation is often considered an undesirable side reaction during mixed aldol condensation. However, it is a spontaneous and thermodynamically favored process. To avoid this reaction, specific precautions must be taken during experimental procedures.
